newsitem.title: USA: Richmond Fed's Owens sees tight labor, wage gains.
newsitem.headline: Richmond Fed's Owens sees tight labor, wage gains.

text.p: Labor markets in the Richmond Federal Reserve district continue to tighten, bringing higher wages, Richmond Fed economist Raymond Owens said Tuesday.
"The labor markets are extremely tight across the region and our (May) survey indicates that there's some further tightening in prospect for those," Owens told Reuters Financial Television.
"We're beginning now to see fairly strong increases in the wage indexes as well," Owens added.
For the months ahead, survey respondents "are still looking for some further additions to their workforce and perhaps that would lead to some additional tightening in labor markets," Owens said.
Owens added that inflation is beginning to creep higher in the district across manufacturing, services and retail businesses.
"Now, that's not true of every category every month, but clearly a trend seems to be beginning of a very modest creep up of prices," said Owens.
Owens declined to say the upcreep could lead to higher official inflation measures and added that the solid pace of economic growth seen through March of this year seems to have continued into May.

"What these (survey) reports do suggest is that the strong surge in growth that we saw back in March is largely being maintained. It's perhaps moderating a little bit, but the economy here apparently is still growing at a very high level, though it's not accelerating further," he added.
